plain: To make a law, claim or contract no longer valid

webster.text: To weaken or lessen the force of; more generally, to destroy the strength or validity of; to render of no force or effect; as, to invalidate an agreement or a contract.

example.quote: bill cannot be admitted, because they would invalidate that right, why may it
example.cite: James Madison, Speech in Congress Opposing the National Bank, Feb. 2, 1791
